_meta.title: Eclipse 2026-08-12 — magnetic bucket post-event evaluation (DRAFT for decider/curmudgeon review; not yet OTS-anchored)
_meta.status: DRAFT — requires curmudgeon adversarial pass + operator approval + independent OTS stamp per post_event_protocol step 6

headline: The magnetic sub-test did not deliver a clean verdict for either model, and it did not confirm the dome. Raw magnetometer deviations of -13 to -19 nT look like a dome hit, but the same depression was present two hours before the eclipse began and tracks a storm-recovery ring-current offset (Dst ~12-15 nT below the quiet-day baseline). Once that is removed, the eclipse-attributable signal at every pre-registered station is within about +/-5 nT of zero — far from the dome's -10 nT (frozen formula), -17 to -21 nT (PRED-095/TIER-1) or -28.9 nT (dome live scoring) — and the dips that do exist are simultaneous across 30 degrees of longitude rather than following the Moon's shadow. Our own standard-physics amplitude range (-5 to -25 nT) also looks too high for a sunset eclipse; we say so.

conditions.preregistered_kp_lt_2_met: PARTIAL — met 16:00-18:00 UT, NOT met 18:00-21:00 UT (Kp 2+). Every station's +/-60 min evaluation window (max-coverage times 17:58-18:54 UT) straddles the 18:00 boundary. Strictly, the Kp<2 precondition of B1-M-001, OBS-D-02, OBS-D-04 and OBS-S-02 is NOT satisfied for any station.
conditions.geomagnetic_context: Storm on 2026-08-08 (Kp 6-, Dst min -59 nT); 2026-08-12 is recovery-phase. Kyoto realtime (quick-look) Dst, eclipse-day minus quiet-day-set mean: -12.0 (16-17UT), -11.6 (17-18UT), -13.8 (18-19UT), -15.0 (19-20UT) nT. Source https://wdc.kugi.kyoto-u.ac.jp/dst_realtime/202608/index.html (quick-look, subject to revision).

methods.data: INTERMAGNET 1-minute data via BGS GIN web service (https://imag-data.bgs.ac.uk/GIN_V1/GINServices, publicationState=best-avail, per-day requests), 2026-07-13..2026-08-12. H = recorded H, or sqrt(X^2+Y^2) for XYZ-reporting observatories. Fetched 2026-09-26.
methods.obscuration: Computed, not taken from the NASA web calculator: skyfield 1.55 + JPL DE421 topocentric apparent Sun/Moon, WGS84 station coordinates from IAGA-2002 headers, area-overlap of the solar disc at 1-min cadence 15:00-21:00 UT. Validation: greatest eclipse reproduced at 17:45 UT at 65.225N/25.228W with obscuration 1.0 (NASA 17:45:53.8); 2017-08-21 Boulder max at 17:46 UT, 93.6% (matches published local circumstances within ~1 pp). Deviation from the protocol (which named the NASA local-circumstances calculator) is disclosed; an independent NASA-calculator cross-check is recommended before publication.
methods.quiet_days: Protocol step 2 read as: days with max 3-h Kp <= 1 in the 30 days preceding the event, ties/fill by lowest daily Kp sum. Only 4 days satisfy max Kp<=1 (07-19, 07-20, 08-01, 08-06); 5th filled with 08-05 (sum 3.33). Sensitivity set ranked purely by daily sum: 08-06, 08-05, 08-07, 07-19, 08-01. Baseline = per-UT-minute mean over quiet days (finer than the protocol's "same UT-hour"; the difference is sub-nT for this window).
methods.protocol_metric: Peak = max |signed deviation| in +/-60 min around each station's computed max-coverage minute (exact protocol step 2).
methods.supplementary_metric_NOT_PREREGISTERED: Eclipse-isolating detrend: fit a line to the deviation over [first contact-60 min, first contact] and [last contact, last contact+60 min], subtract, report mean residual over [t_max-30, t_max+30]. Empirical null = the same statistic on the same UT windows on every non-quiet day of the preceding 30 days with Kp(15-21UT) <= 2.67 (n=13-19 per station). Sensitivity: anchor 30 vs 60 min, linear vs quadratic.

OBS_D_02.detail: Protocol metric: |obs - dome central| > 2 nT at 6 of 7 evaluable dome stations (HAD 1.6 nT is the exception; GUI protocol metric invalid; COI no data). Detrended metric: > 2 nT at 8 of 8 (GUI usable). Quorum >=5/9 met under both metrics. Formal status: Kp<2 precondition not met, so this is a conditions-qualified firing, not a clean pre-registered falsification.

OBS_D_03.note: Dome coverage and computed obscuration are rank-correlated at r12=0.978 across the 7 stations, so the paired test has essentially no power at n=7. The "Borrowed" trilemma branch is not empirically separable with this station set.

OBS_D_04.result: Fires only under the raw protocol metric (all dome stations -13.7..-18.7 nT) which is dominated by a pre-existing ring-current offset; does NOT fire under the eclipse-isolating metric (no dome station residual in [-25,-5]). Kp precondition unmet. Treat as NOT FIRED.

OBS_S_02.detail: Criterion requires |peak| < 1 nT at all high-obscuration stations; raw peaks are 13-19 nT and detrended residual extrema are +/-6-11 nT (ULF/substorm variability).

criteria.OBS_S_03: NOT EVALUATED — no independent observed per-station obscuration measurements; computed values are themselves standard-physics predictions.

OBS_O_01.detail: No station observed < -50 nT (GUI -92 nT protocol value is a publication-state baseline artifact, disclosed). Detrended residuals at 6 northern stations are slightly positive (+0.6..+1.9 nT) but within null noise (|z|<0.7).

OBS_O_02.result: PARTIAL — methodology limit we must publicly note
OBS_O_02.detail: An unanticipated measurement condition (storm-recovery ring-current depression of ~12-15 nT spanning the whole window, plus globally simultaneous dips at 17:09 and 18:47 UT) contaminates both models' signals identically. Per OBS-O-02 wording, our claim that 2026-08-12 is a clean magnetic test of either model is weakened and we must say so.

OBS_O_03.detail: Dome central values not matched within 2 nT at dome stations; candidate stations all show comparable raw deviations.

PRED_095.raw_protocol: 2 of 7 evaluable dome stations in range (ESK -18.7, LER -18.1); 0 of 5 candidate stations; alt quiet-day set 3 of 7 (SPT, ESK, LER). Majority of >80% stations outside range under both baselines.
PRED_095.eclipse_isolated: No station within 10 nT of the range; residuals -3.2..+1.9 nT at dome stations.
PRED_095.assessment: Not confirmed under any metric; appears partially confirmed only by counting a storm-recovery offset that was already present 14:00-16:00 UT before first contact anywhere in Europe.

PRED_TIER_1.claim: -17 to -21 nT umbra-locked at >=3 priority stations
PRED_TIER_1.assessment: FAILS independent of Kp: (a) raw protocol peaks reach the range at only 2 dome stations with the primary baseline; (b) all raw peaks are NOT umbra-locked — they occur simultaneously (within ~2 min) at 17:09 and 18:46-18:48 UT across Iberia to Romania (~30 deg longitude) while the stations' max-coverage times span 17:58-18:54 UT; LER's peak (17:25) precedes its max coverage by 33 min. Umbra-locked timing is the claim's own discriminator and it is absent.

verbatim.name: Eclipse Magnetic Anomaly (Aug 12 2026)
verbatim.falsification: Fails if measured anomaly within ±3 nT of 0

dome_live_scoring_entry.assessment: Dome's own live criterion: predicted -28.9 nT at EBR/SPT, falsification "measured anomaly within +/-3 nT of 0". Raw protocol: EBR -13.7, SPT -15.6 (miss the -28.9 prediction by 15-13 nT, ~47-53%, but pass the dome's one-sided zero test). Eclipse-isolated: EBR -2.2 (inside +/-3 nT -> FAILS the dome's own rule), SPT -3.2 (marginal); across 6 detrend variants EBR is inside +/-3 nT in 5, SPT in 4. The dome's own verdict therefore hinges entirely on whether the storm-recovery offset is subtracted. Note also the dome asserts globe_prediction = 0.0, a strawman: Chapman-Sq predicts a non-zero, conductivity-scaled effect. Formula inconsistency: live scoring uses baseline -18.22 nT (present since the first status_history record 2026-04-05) while the V51.1 formula table/9-station table used in our frozen bucket 2 uses -10.9 nT.

self_corrections.finding: Under the eclipse-isolating metric no pre-registered station shows an eclipse-attributable dip of >=5 nT (dome stations -3.2..+1.9; best case non-registered SFS -5.0). Our standard-physics range was drawn from daytime-eclipse ensembles (Kim & Chang 2018) and was not scaled for a near-sunset eclipse (Sun 5-14 deg altitude at max coverage; E-region/Sq conductivity already low). Kp precondition unmet so this is not a formal falsification of B1-M-001, but the honesty clause obliges us to publish that our range looks miscalibrated high, not that the data confirmed it.

self_corrections.item: Frozen-file sign convention (uniform negative) and OBS-O-01 positive-value trigger
self_corrections.finding: Standard Sq physics predicts a latitude-dependent sign relative to the Sq current focus; a uniform negative sign for all European stations was over-specified. Observed detrended residuals are negative in Iberia and weakly positive further north — within noise, so not evidence either way, but the frozen convention should be flagged as a known limitation in the results addendum.

self_corrections.item: B1-G-005 Hartland peak obscuration 88% +/-2 pp (and review §4.2.7 "~2 h 45 min" partial duration)
self_corrections.finding: DE421/skyfield computation gives 94.4% at 18:15 UT with partial phase 17:18-19:08 UT (~1 h 50 min). Needs independent confirmation against the NASA local-circumstances calculator before any prose edit; if confirmed, our frozen value was ~6 pp low (outside its own +/-2 pp bound) — record in the results addendum, do not edit the frozen file.

Our pre-registered evaluation target was 2026-09-11; this evaluation ran 2026-09-26 (15 days late) because the pipeline was paused. The review has been citing the dome's post-close silence; we should disclose our own lateness in the results file rather than let it be found.
